STATUS: HAND ADJUDICATION WITH RECEIPTS — the stopping rule's declared endpoint
why_not_a_third_lexicon: widening again against known misses would be fitting the rule to the data. Two mechanical passes, then eyes on the field.

DECOMPOSITION.why: the region exists and is plural but is NOT coordinate-shaped — blend operations are coordinate-wise and a majority vote of three tree decompositions has no meaning
DECOMPOSITION.re_entry: any faithful fixed-length encoding someone declares falsifies this
DECOMPOSITION.the_irony_worth_recording: the width parameters are parameterized complexity's OWN structural yardsticks. The observatory currently cannot film the very objects the param charge is built on.

STRATEGY.why: a sequence of choices against a spreading process
STRATEGY.distinct_from_RECONFIGURATION: walking between solutions is not playing against dynamics
STRATEGY.re_entry: WARMER than DECOMPOSITION's: a fixed-horizon strategy IS a length-T vector (round -> choice), so a faithful fixed-length encoding plausibly exists. The barrier is the dynamic feasibility predicate, not the shape — nearest of the out-of-reach classes to capturable.

counting_correction: sharp-spanning-trees and planar-matching-count are REACH-SUBSET, not a counting limbo. The # changes what the CHARGE asks, not whether the object has a region: spanning trees and matchings are edge-subset regions and film like any other. These are the first rows where the decide-versus-count geometric comparison becomes physically possible.

coexisting_different_axis.resolution: BOTH STAND — different axes, no supersession
BOTH STAND — different axes, no supersession

reconciliation_rule: one row, one current typing ON EACH AXIS. A competing REACH CLASS resolves by maptrail supersession — latest ruling governs, histories linked, neither deleted. A prior CAPTURE disposition is not a competing typing and both stand: what an object IS and whether the observatory can film it are different questions, and collapsing them would retire a live deferral by accident.

rows.why: one shortest-path matrix; the answer is unique
rows.canonical_encoding: weighted graph; shortest path between every pair

rows.why: accessibility of a fixed target under fixed semantics; unique
rows.canonical_encoding: an AND/OR graph with a source set; decision: is a target vertex accessible (AND-vertices need all in-neighbors, OR-vertices any)?

rows.why: same, with capacities binding the map
rows.canonical_encoding: a metric on facilities and clients, facility opening costs, and facility capacities (max clients per open facility); objective = minimize (sum of opening costs + sum of client-to-assigned-facility distances) respecting capacities

rows.why: a clique-width expression (a parse tree over union/relabel/join)
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = minimum number of labels k in a clique-width expression (using disjoint union, relabelling, and label-join operations) that constructs G

rows.why: an s-t path under a resource budget; ordered
rows.canonical_encoding: a directed graph with two nonnegative edge functions cost and resource, a source, a target, and a resource budget R; objective = minimum-cost s-t path whose total resource use is <= R

rows.why: words within the radius of the code
rows.canonical_encoding: a binary linear code given by an m x n parity-check matrix H over GF(2) (C = {x : x H^T = 0}); integer r; covering radius rho = max_{x in {0,1}^n} min_{c in C} d(x,c) (Hamming distance)

rows.why: a yes/no property of one fixed graph; no plural certificate
rows.canonical_encoding: a single-unit resource-allocation graph; decision: is the system deadlocked (an unresolvable wait cycle)?

rows.why: arc subset forming an arborescence
rows.canonical_encoding: directed edge-weighted graph + root + terminals; min-cost arborescence reaching terminals

rows.why: open set PLUS the client-to-facility map the objective scores
rows.canonical_encoding: a metric on facilities and clients, and facility opening costs (no capacity limits); objective = minimize (sum of opening costs of opened facilities + sum of each client's distance to its nearest opened facility)

rows.why: arc subset whose removal breaks all cycles
rows.canonical_encoding: simple directed graph, adjacency-list; objective = minimum arc set whose removal makes G acyclic

rows.why: a per-round protection choice against a spreading fire
rows.canonical_encoding: rooted tree, one firefighter per round protecting one vertex; fire spreads to unprotected neighbours; objective = maximize number of vertices saved (never burned)

rows.why: jobs to machine-slots
rows.canonical_encoding: n jobs, each processed on 3 machines in the fixed order M1->M2->M3 with given processing times; objective = minimize makespan (Cmax)

rows.why: sign vectors over the coordinates
rows.canonical_encoding: two integer vectors u, v (binary-encoded) of equal length n and an integer target t; x, y range over {0,1}^n

rows.why: a per-round ignition choice against a spreading burn
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph; in each round the existing fire spreads to all neighbours and one new vertex is ignited; objective = minimum #rounds (burning number b(G)) to burn every vertex

rows.why: vertex subset realizing the colour multiset
rows.canonical_encoding: vertex-colored graph + multiset of colors; connected subgraph realizing the multiset

rows.why: edge subset meeting a stretch guarantee
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected unweighted graph; objective = minimum-edge spanning subgraph H such that d_H(u,v) <= 2*d_G(u,v) for all u,v (a 2-spanner)

rows.why: edge subset touching every group
rows.canonical_encoding: edge-weighted graph + vertex groups; minimum tree touching every group

rows.why: vertex subset inducing minimum degree >= k
rows.canonical_encoding: a graph G and integer k>=3; decision: does G have a nonempty induced subgraph of minimum degree >= k (does a given vertex survive the k-core-style peeling)?

rows.why: operations to slots
rows.canonical_encoding: n jobs, m machines, operation orders + times in binary; minimize makespan

rows.why: centre set of size k
rows.canonical_encoding: metric on n points (distance matrix); decision: cover with k radius-r balls?

rows.why: edge subset that is k-edge-connected
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph G and integer k; objective = minimum-cardinality spanning subgraph that is k-edge-connected (unweighted, uniform requirement)

rows.why: a labelling of the vertices from label sets
rows.canonical_encoding: bipartite constraint graph, label sets L_U,L_V, each edge carrying a projection constraint pi_e: L_U->L_V; objective = a labelling maximizing the fraction of satisfied edges (the two-prover / PCP projection game)

rows.why: UNIQUE given the fixed edge order the encoding states — the exact twin of lex-first-maximal-independent-set, reached by a different door (unmatched rather than false-matched)
rows.canonical_encoding: a graph with a fixed edge order and an edge e; decision: is e in the lexicographically-first maximal matching (greedy in order)?

rows.why: a simple path is an ordered walk; the sequence is the certificate
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; decision: simple path of length >= k?

rows.why: jobs to machines
rows.canonical_encoding: n job lengths in binary + m machines; decision: makespan <= T?

rows.why: subset of the set system
rows.canonical_encoding: set system + budget k; decision: k sets covering >= t elements?

rows.why: edge subset removed to leave agreeing components
rows.canonical_encoding: two rooted binary phylogenetic trees on the same leaf label set; objective = an agreement forest with the fewest components (equivalently the rooted SPR distance = #components - 1)

rows.why: a partial isomorphism — a map between two vertex sets
rows.canonical_encoding: two graphs; find the largest graph isomorphic to a subgraph of both

rows.why: a SUBSYSTEM is a subset of the relations
rows.canonical_encoding: a system of linear relations (equations/inequalities) with rational coefficients that is infeasible as a whole; objective = maximum-cardinality subsystem that is feasible

rows.why: edge subset that induces no further edges
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph; an induced matching is a matching M whose edges induce no other edges (pairwise at distance >= 2); objective = maximum |M|

rows.why: edge subset forming a spanning tree
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph; spanning tree with >= k leaves

rows.why: edge subset forming a spanning tree
rows.canonical_encoding: connected graph with metric edge lengths; uniform (unit) communication requirement between every vertex pair; objective = spanning tree T minimizing routing cost = sum over all pairs of the T-path length (minimum routing cost spanning tree, MRCT). Encoding PIN: the uniform-requirement metric special case of the Optimum Communication Spanning Tree (OCT)

rows.why: a min-cost flow value; the optimum is unique even where the flow is not
rows.canonical_encoding: directed graph with capacities + costs (binary); min-cost feasible flow

rows.why: edge subset forming a spanning tree
rows.canonical_encoding: simple connected graph, adjacency-list; objective = spanning tree minimizing the maximum vertex degree

rows.why: certificate is a decision TREE over the tests, not a subset of them
rows.canonical_encoding: a set of objects and a set of binary tests (each test splits the objects); objective = a decision tree of minimum cost (e.g. minimum total external path length / expected #tests) that identifies every object

rows.why: nonzero messages of bounded codeword weight
rows.canonical_encoding: a linear code over a finite field given by a generator or parity-check matrix; objective = the minimum Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword (the minimum distance)

rows.why: edge subset whose removal leaves k components
rows.canonical_encoding: undirected graph with edge weights and an integer k (part of the input, no fixed terminals); objective = a minimum-weight set of edges whose removal leaves at least k connected components

rows.why: edge subset separating every pair
rows.canonical_encoding: undirected graph with edge weights and a set of source-sink terminal pairs; objective = a minimum-weight set of edges whose removal disconnects every terminal pair

rows.why: edge subset separating the terminals
rows.canonical_encoding: edge-weighted graph + terminal set; separate all terminals minimizing cut

rows.why: messages within a distance of the target
rows.canonical_encoding: a linear code over GF(2) given by a generator matrix, and a target vector y; objective = a codeword minimizing the Hamming distance to y (maximum-likelihood decoding)

rows.why: VERTEX subset separating the terminals
rows.canonical_encoding: undirected graph and a set of >= 3 terminals; objective = a minimum-cardinality set of non-terminal vertices whose removal pairwise separates all terminals

rows.why: operations to machines, order free
rows.canonical_encoding: n jobs and m machines (m part of the input); each job has one operation per machine, executable in any order but not concurrently; objective = minimize the makespan (O||Cmax)

rows.why: path decomposition — same shape
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph; objective = the minimum width over all path-decompositions (equivalently interval-completion clique number minus one / vertex separation number)

rows.why: matchings are edge subsets; the # joins at the atlas layer
rows.canonical_encoding: planar graph, adjacency-list; count perfect matchings

rows.why: edge subset; penalties score the complement
rows.canonical_encoding: edge-weighted graph + vertex penalties; minimize tree weight + unconnected penalties

rows.why: an evaluation ORDER of the DAG
rows.canonical_encoding: a directed acyclic graph (an expression/computation DAG); decision: can the DAG be evaluated using at most k registers (Sethi register-sufficiency / black pebble game)?

rows.why: jobs to machines under resource bounds
rows.canonical_encoding: n unit/known-length jobs on m identical machines with s shared renewable resources (per-job resource demands, per-resource bounds); minimize makespan

rows.why: assigns 0/1/2 per vertex; a three-valued labelling, not a subset
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph; a Roman dominating function assigns 0/1/2 to vertices so every 0-vertex is adjacent to a 2-vertex; objective = minimum total weight

rows.why: COUNTING changes what the charge asks, not whether the object has a region — the set of spanning trees IS an edge-subset region
rows.canonical_encoding: connected undirected (multi)graph, adjacency-list; count the spanning trees of G

rows.why: the cut is a vertex bipartition — recorded as a subset of one side
rows.canonical_encoding: a capacitated graph with a set of source-sink demand pairs; find a cut minimizing the ratio of cut capacity to separated demand (non-uniform sparsest cut)

rows.why: a matching IS a map between the two sides
rows.canonical_encoding: two sides with preference lists; find a stable matching

rows.why: edge subset connecting each pair
rows.canonical_encoding: edge-weighted graph + terminal PAIRS; connect each pair minimizing total weight

rows.why: edge subset forming a tree over the terminals
rows.canonical_encoding: edge-weighted graph + terminal set; decision: Steiner tree of weight <= B?

rows.why: edge subset meeting connectivity requirements
rows.canonical_encoding: edge-weighted graph + connectivity requirements r(u,v); min-cost subgraph meeting them

rows.why: the seed set is a vertex subset
rows.canonical_encoding: a graph with per-vertex thresholds; an initially active seed set activates a neighbor once its number of active neighbors reaches its threshold; find the minimum seed set activating the whole graph

rows.why: elimination forest — same shape
rows.canonical_encoding: graph; minimum height of an elimination forest, <= k

rows.why: certificate is a tree decomposition; blend is coordinate-wise and a majority of three tree decompositions has no meaning
rows.canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; decision: treewidth <= k?

rows.why: jobs to machines with machine-dependent times
rows.canonical_encoding: n jobs and m machines with a machine-dependent processing time p_ij for each job-machine pair; assign jobs to machines minimizing the makespan

rows.why: jobs to machines
rows.canonical_encoding: n jobs with processing times and weights, m identical parallel machines; minimize the weighted sum of job completion times sum_j w_j C_j
